text: An event page for Bengaluru JS Meetup in November: schedule, speakers, RSVP, venue and map, code of conduct, and sponsor logos.

@CEO the brief leaves three choices open that change risk or external commitment: how unconfirmed facts are handled, what RSVP does, and how the map is provided. Everything in the brief (schedule, speakers, RSVP, venue and map, code of conduct, sponsor logos) stays in scope whichever options you pick.
1. The brief gives no confirmed speakers, talk times, venue address, date or sponsor names. How should the page treat content we do not have?
   Option 1: Use clearly marked placeholder content (e.g. 'Speaker TBA', sample times) in every section so the full page is reviewable now. Consequence: the Requester sees the complete layout immediately. Risk: invented-looking details could be mistaken for real ones and published unchanged.
   Option 2: Build every section with real structure but show only 'To be announced' text where facts are missing, with no sample names or times. Consequence: nothing false can appear on the page. Risk: the page looks sparse and the Requester has less to judge visually.
   Option 3: Pause for the Requester to supply the real facts before building any section. Consequence: the first version contains accurate content. Risk: the run stalls until the Requester replies, and the build starts later.
2. The site is a single static file with no server. What should the RSVP section do?
   Option 1: Link out to an external RSVP page the Requester already uses (e.g. Meetup, Luma, Google Form). Consequence: real sign-ups are collected and no attendee data touches our page. Risk: we need the Requester to supply the link, and attendees leave the page.
   Option 2: Embed a form that submits to a third-party form service. Consequence: sign-ups happen on the page itself. Risk: attendee names and emails go to an outside service the Requester must set up and approve, which adds a privacy and data-handling duty.
   Option 3: Use a 'mailto:' button that opens an email to an organiser address. Consequence: works with no external service. Risk: relies on the attendee having a mail app configured, so some sign-ups will be lost and the organiser must count replies by hand.
3. How should the venue and map be shown?
   Option 1: Embed an interactive Google Maps frame plus a text address. Consequence: familiar, easy to navigate. Risk: loads a third-party script that sets cookies and can show an error if the embed is blocked or the venue is not found.
   Option 2: Embed an OpenStreetMap-based map (e.g. Leaflet via CDN) plus a text address. Consequence: no Google account or API key is needed. Risk: place search and transit detail are weaker, and the venue pin must be set from exact coordinates the Requester confirms.
   Option 3: Show the text address with a 'Get directions' link that opens the map app, with no embedded map. Consequence: lightest and most reliable page, nothing third-party loads. Risk: the brief's 'map' may be read as not met because the page shows no map inline.

@Identity Decisions: 1 is option 2 (no invented facts), 2 is option 1 (link out), 3 is option 2 (OpenStreetMap map). Adaptation should build all six sections, with missing facts and the RSVP link tracked as open inputs for the Requester and none of them blocking done.
1. The brief gives no confirmed speakers, talk times, venue address, date or sponsor names. How should the page treat content we do not have? Build every section with real structure but show only 'To be announced' text where facts are missing, with no sample names or times. Consequence: nothing false can appear on the page. Risk: the page looks sparse and the Requester has less to judge visually. (The brief gives no speakers, times, venue, date or sponsors, and invented sample details could be published as if real, so show 'To be announced' with real section structure and keep the Requester's missing facts as open inputs.)
2. The site is a single static file with no server. What should the RSVP section do? Link out to an external RSVP page the Requester already uses (e.g. Meetup, Luma, Google Form). Consequence: real sign-ups are collected and no attendee data touches our page. Risk: we need the Requester to supply the link, and attendees leave the page. (A link to the Requester's own RSVP page collects real sign-ups with no attendee data on our page and no privacy duty; the brief is silent on the link, so show a clearly marked placeholder button until the Requester supplies it.)
3. How should the venue and map be shown? Embed an OpenStreetMap-based map (e.g. Leaflet via CDN) plus a text address. Consequence: no Google account or API key is needed. Risk: place search and transit detail are weaker, and the venue pin must be set from exact coordinates the Requester confirms. (The brief asks for a map, so an inline map is needed, and Leaflet with OpenStreetMap shows one without cookies or an API key; accepted trade-off is weaker place search, and until the Requester confirms the venue the map shows a Bengaluru city view with no pin and a 'venue to be announced' note.)

@Priority two workflows: W1 builds the single-file page with every section as 'To be announced' placeholders, W2 adds the Venue section and Leaflet/OSM map. Total 45 of 50. Sections are grouped into 3 page_section units to fit the budget, which leaves only 5 and no room for a fix (8).

proposal.name: Build single-file event page with placeholder sections
proposal.goal_gap: No page exists. Needs one HTML file titled and headed 'Bengaluru JS Meetup', stating the event is in November, with Schedule, Speakers, Sponsors, RSVP and Code of Conduct sections.
proposal.expected_outcome: One HTML file with inline CSS and JS. All facts read 'To be announced'. RSVP is a marked placeholder link button with no form or input fields. Code of Conduct shows a heading and a marked 'text to be announced' placeholder. Sponsors shows logo slots marked 'To be announced' with no image sources.
proposal.completion_check: File has 'Bengaluru JS Meetup' in the title and h1, and 'November' in the text. It has Schedule, Speakers, Sponsors, RSVP and Code of Conduct sections. Every schedule slot, talk and speaker entry reads 'To be announced'. There is no form or input element. The RSVP control is marked placeholder. There are no personal names, times, exact dates, sponsor names or image src values.

proposal.name: Add Venue section and Leaflet OpenStreetMap map
proposal.goal_gap: The page has no Venue section and no map.
proposal.expected_outcome: Venue section in the same file with the text address 'To be announced', a visible 'venue to be announced' note, and a Leaflet map using OpenStreetMap tiles from a CDN, centred on Bengaluru with no marker.
proposal.completion_check: File loads Leaflet from a CDN with OpenStreetMap tile URLs and creates a map centred on Bengaluru with no marker call. The Venue section has the address text 'To be announced' and the note 'venue to be announced'. There is no Google Maps embed or API key.
